symptom: Re-running a `create or modify workflow` whose workflow has an interrupting timer boundary event, the same script that created it, failed: 'workflow … has 2 stored `end workflow` inside its branches but this statement declares 0'. Found on 11.17.0 while working on #2616, and present on 11.16.1 with mxcli main: every workflow with an interrupting boundary event could be created once and never re-applied.
cause: An interrupting boundary event's path always ends the workflow: the writer appends an EndWorkflowActivity, and Studio Pro normalizes an interrupting path to one. MDL never states it. The guard subtracted the main flow's End and each event sub-process's closing End as implicit, but not this one, so it counted as a dropped `end workflow`.
fix: rawImplicitBoundaryEnds subtracts the End that closes each interrupting boundary event's path. An End a branch really states is still counted.
insight: A rewrite guard that counts stored nodes has to subtract every node the writer adds on its own. When a new kind of implicit node appears (boundary path terminators here, sub-process ends before), the guard silently becomes 'refuse every re-run'. Re-running the creating script is the cheapest test for it, and the doctype gate does not do that.
test: mdl/executor/validate_workflow_rewrite_boundary_end_test.go (a restating statement passes; control: a stored branch End is still refused); failed before with the reported message
